name: How much contingency should I keep for a Los Angeles new build?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I set aside for unexpected costs in a Los Angeles new home construction project?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I set aside for unexpected costs in a Los Angeles new home construction project?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency reserve is essential in Los Angeles new construction because site conditions and permit requirements can change the budget even when the original plan looks complete. Unexpected grading, utility upgrades, soil issues, code-related changes, and owner-requested upgrades are common causes of extra spending. Projects on hillside lots, tight urban lots, or properties with older infrastructure usually need a larger reserve than flat, straightforward sites. The best way to manage this is to separate the base contract from allowances and contingency so you can see how much of your budget is truly committed. Ask your builder which risks are already included and which are not. That clarity helps you avoid running out of money after the foundation or framing phase, when changes become much more expensive.
acceptedAnswer.description: A contingency reserve is usually needed because site conditions, permit revisions, utility upgrades, and material changes can raise the final cost. Many homeowners set aside extra funds beyond the base contract to cover surprises. Projects on hillside or older urban lots typically need a larger contingency.
